implementerProof.how: Round three answers the review's request for changes (one High, two Medium, nine minors at e7e4a6af). The implement handoff now carries fourteen proofs at the fix head 02b80896702e, three of them for the review's findings. Each was re-driven here on a live pair rebuilt at that tree — packages/envoy/scripts/dev-broker.sh and packages/dispatch `bun run dispatch:local`, with a counting proxy between Dispatch and the broker — by the same second DPoP/RFC 8693 client written from the RFCs with the Go standard library alone, never internal/broker/helper. The three findings are closed on the surface, not only in a test: (1) every uuid spelling Postgres accepts but Go's uuid.Parse refuses — no hyphens, a hyphen after each group of four, uppercase, braces — now resolves another project's comment to its project and is refused 403 PROJECT_SCOPE, while the same spellings of the caller's own comment still work, so the resolver and the handler agree in both directions; (2) a machine login's own access token, which the broker answers live with no session, is refused 401 BROKER_TOKEN_NOT_A_SESSION at whoami and at every write, and the request body no longer chooses the session, while that same token still exchanges for a session-bearing one; (3) an upload or message into another session's conversation is refused 403 SESSION_SCOPE naming both sessions, while the caller's own session is accepted. The review's minors I could drive are fixed too: the rate refusal is now 429 with Retry-After: 1, and a project-scoped caller naming an external ref mapped to another project is refused before anything is returned or recorded. Every acceptance line of rounds one and two was re-driven at this head and still holds.

proof.criterion: The review's High finding is closed: a project-scoped token cannot reach another project's object by spelling its id the way Postgres accepts and Go's uuid.Parse does not (INFRA-265).
proof.surface: The live pair at the fix tree: POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/reply and the other id-addressed rows, with one EXAMPLE-scoped broker token, against a comment of the seed's CORE and against one of EXAMPLE.
proof.command: The CORE comment 199c4663-da1e-4034-8b76-35e09bca7c03 addressed five ways — canonical, no hyphens (199c4663da1e40348b7635e09bca7c03), a hyphen after each group of four (199c-4663-da1e-4034-8b76-35e0-9bca-7c03), uppercase, and braces ({…}, percent-encoded) — then the CORE ask and the CORE document in the four-group form, then the EXAMPLE comment in each of those spellings
proof.observed: All five spellings of the CORE comment → 403 PROJECT_SCOPE 'this request's credential may write project EXAMPLE; this write belongs to project CORE'; the CORE ask and CORE document in the four-group form → the same refusal. The same four spellings of the caller's own EXAMPLE comment → 200 each, so nothing honest broke: the check resolves exactly what the handler resolves.
proof.negativeControl: The caller's own comment in the no-hyphen and four-group spellings is accepted in the same run, so the refusal is the project and not the spelling; and an id that resolves to nothing (an unknown uuid, a non-uuid) is refused 403 'this write resolves to no project of that credential's' rather than answered, which is the fail-closed rule the review asked for.

proof.criterion: The review's first Medium is closed: a live broker token that names no session is refused, and the request body cannot fill one in (INFRA-264).
proof.surface: The live pair: a person's machine login driven by hand at the broker (device authorization with an RFC 9101 request object and dpop_jkt, approved through agent-secrets-devrelay, the device code redeemed), whose own access token — not an exchanged one — is then presented to Dispatch.
proof.command: POST /v1/oauth/introspect on the machine access token; then GET /api/v1/whoami, POST /api/v1/issues with a body actor naming ses-chosen-by-the-body, and POST /api/v1/issues/CORE-1/comments with the same body actor, each under 'Authorization: DPoP <that machine token>'
proof.observed: The broker answers {"active":true,"scope":"machine","client_id":"agent-secrets-helper"} — live, and naming no session and no person. Dispatch refuses all three with 401 BROKER_TOKEN_NOT_A_SESSION 'this access token is not a session's credential: the secrets broker names no session for it'. Nothing is created and no session is taken from the body.
proof.negativeControl: The same machine token still exchanges for a session-bearing token in the same run (POST /v1/oauth/token, subject_token_type access_token, session ada-devbox → 200), and that token is accepted at whoami, so the refusal is the missing session and not the token or its key.

proof.criterion: The review's second Medium is closed: a route that writes into one session's conversation is held to the session the credential proved (INFRA-265).
proof.surface: The live pair: POST /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/artifacts and POST /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/messages under a broker token proving session example-worker-session.
proof.command: A multipart upload into the seeded planner's session 019a1c01-0d7b-7a2a-8e93-4a5b6c7d8e01, then the identical upload into example-worker-session, then a message into the planner's session
proof.observed: The other session's conversation → 403 SESSION_SCOPE 'this request's credential acts for session example-worker-session; POST /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/artifacts writes into session 019a1c01-…'; its own session → 201 with the artifact recorded under agent/example-worker-session/mine-txt; the message route → the same 403 naming itself.
proof.negativeControl: The caller's own session is accepted in the same run, and the shared token on the same route still answers its old 400 ACTOR_KIND ('bearer callers require actor.kind session'), so the new check leaves every credential that proves no session exactly as it was.

proof.criterion: A caller presenting a broker-issued token is accepted and Dispatch reports the session, the person and the project; a mismatching body actor, an unprovable key, a replayed proof and the Bearer scheme are each refused (INFRA-264).
proof.command: GET /api/v1/whoami under DPoP; POST /api/v1/issues/EXAMPLE-1/comments with no actor, a matching actor and an actor naming ses-not-mine; the same whoami under Bearer, proved by a second key, and with one jti presented twice
proof.observed: 200 {"kind":"agent","owner":"ada@example.com","project":"EXAMPLE","service":null,"session":"example-worker-session"}; the writes 201, 201 and 403 ACTOR_SESSION_MISMATCH; Bearer → 401 UNAUTHORIZED; the second key → 401 BROKER_TOKEN_KEY_MISMATCH; the replayed jti → 401 BROKER_TOKEN_PROOF_INVALID.
proof.negativeControl: The accepted writes in the same run, so each refusal is the one thing it names.

proof.criterion: A revoked token stops working within the cache's few seconds, and a refusal is never served from a cache, on an exchanged token and on a dev box token (INFRA-264; the architect's point 4).
proof.surface: The same live pair with the counting proxy.
proof.command: whoami to cache the answer, POST /v1/oauth/revoke as the dispatch caller, then whoami every half second; and, for the dev box token, POST /v1/launcher-credentials/{id}/revoke-by-approver after the same caching read
proof.observed: Exchanged token: accepted to t=+4.7 s, 401 BROKER_TOKEN_NOT_ACTIVE at t=+5.3 s, the window costing two introspections. Dev box token (project_scope person, whoami project null, writing both projects as the rule says): accepted to t=+4.7 s, refused at t=+5.2 s. A refusal is never cached: one unknown token presented twice cost two introspections. The cache and its single flight: five presentations within 1.5 s cost one introspection, a sixth after five seconds a second, and ten concurrent presentations of a fresh token exactly one, all ten answered 200.
proof.negativeControl: Both revocations presented by the introspection-only caller → 403 ACCOUNT_LACKS_POWER naming that caller and that route, with the token still accepted afterwards.

proof.criterion: A write to an object of a project the token does not cover is refused and names both projects, a deployment-wide write is refused by name, and an external ref mapped to another project is refused before anything is returned (INFRA-265, with the review's first minor).
proof.surface: The same live pair, with EXAMPLE as the token's project, the seed's CORE as the other, and a repository mapping acme/widgets → CORE made by a signed-in person.
proof.command: Under one EXAMPLE token: writes to CORE's issue, comment, ask, document and project document; POST /api/v1/projects and POST /api/v1/broadcasts; POST /api/v1/issues with external acme/widgets#1 (an issue the person had already created from that ref) and with acme/widgets#2 (a ref no issue holds yet)
proof.observed: Every CORE address → 403 PROJECT_SCOPE naming both projects; both deployment rows → 403 PROJECT_SCOPE_DEPLOYMENT naming the route; both external refs → 403 PROJECT_SCOPE 'this write belongs to project CORE', so neither the existing CORE-8 nor a related-check record was returned or written.
proof.negativeControl: The person created CORE-8 from the same ref in the same run, and the EXAMPLE token's writes to its own project are accepted, so the refusal is the project and not the ref.

proof.criterion: The rate refusal names how long to wait (the review's second minor), and the unauthenticated path still cannot spend the people's approval budget (plan P5).
proof.surface: The same live pair with the counting proxy.
proof.command: Forty-five presentations of distinct unknown tokens from one address, then one more read with its response headers
proof.observed: 429 Too Many Requests with 'Retry-After: 1' and {"code":"BROKER_TOKEN_RATE_LIMITED","error":"too many access tokens checked from this address; try again in 200ms"}; the tokens past the bucket never reached the broker.
proof.negativeControl: Ten concurrent presentations of one live token in the same stack cost one introspection and all answered 200, so the bound refuses the flood and not the honest caller.

proof.criterion: The document editor's live connection takes a person's cookie and no bearer, and a person's editing is unaffected (INFRA-264, INFRA-265).
proof.surface: The live Dispatch, and the repository's browser suite in a real Chromium against the production SPA build.
proof.command: Upgrade /ws/doc/{EXAMPLE-1's spec} with the shared bearer and the old X-Dispatch-Actor header, and with a signed-in person's cookie; then `bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium e2e/doc.e2e.ts e2e/collab-cursor.e2e.ts` against the same instance
proof.observed: The shared token → 401; the cookie → 101. The browser suite: 17 of 17 rows passed in 2.5 m, two people editing one document live with their cursors, named versions, the diff, an agent edit landing in an open editor, and reconnection after a dropped transport.
proof.negativeControl: The same shared token on the HTTP API in the same run → 200 at /api/v1/whoami, so the socket's 401 is the deleted door.

proof.criterion: An open stream re-resolves its caller without replaying the proof, a multipart body is not eaten, and a broker outage fails closed rather than unscoping the caller.
proof.surface: The live Dispatch: a /ws/live socket under a broker token, a multipart artifact upload, and every route with cmd/broker stopped.
proof.command: A WebSocket held 45 s (three heartbeats) under one proof; POST /api/v1/issues/EXAMPLE-1/artifacts as multipart; then, with the broker killed, whoami, the issue create, a comment on an issue that does not exist, and the agent artifact upload
proof.observed: The socket stayed open the whole 45 s and took two frames; the multipart upload answered 201; with the broker down every one of the four answered 503 BROKER_UNAVAILABLE, the caller's own targets included.
proof.negativeControl: In the same outage the shared token and a person's cookie both answered 200 at /api/v1/whoami, so the 503 is the broker-token branch alone.

proof.criterion: The fix's own tests pass, and the route table still admits no undecided mutating row.
proof.surface: The packages' own suites against a real Postgres at the fix tree.
proof.negativeControl: TestEveryMutatingRouteIsClassed's own sub-tests are the control and pass: the same walk over a fixture holding an unclassed mutating row, and over one classed as a project's write whose address names no object, fails on each.

proof.criterion: The private-name check passes (the repository's own required check).
proof.surface: The repository's own script over this working copy.
proof.observed: exit 0 — 'no file or path names the private deployment repository or the company, and no text names a private internal host or a Tailscale MagicDNS host (6512 files in the repository)'.
proof.negativeControl: none needed: the script's refusal path is the repository's own.

whatWasTriedAndHeld: Every uuid spelling Postgres accepts (none, four-group and braced hyphenation, upper case) against another project's comment, ask and document: refused; against the caller's own: accepted.

A lowercase issue key and a lowercase project key (example-1, /projects/example/...): nobody can address them — a signed-in person gets 404 for both — so the fail-closed 403 a scoped caller would get names no object that works for anyone else, and no honest call is broken by it.
A machine login's own live access token at whoami and at two writes with a body actor: 401 BROKER_TOKEN_NOT_A_SESSION, nothing created.
An upload and a message into another session's conversation: 403 SESSION_SCOPE; the caller's own session accepted.

A proof replayed by jti, one with no ath, one with another token's ath, one whose htu names another origin, one with typ jwt, one with iat ten minutes either side of now, and one signed by a second key: each refused with its own code.
A broker outage on every route, including the caller's own project and the session-scoped routes: 503 BROKER_UNAVAILABLE, never an unscoped write, while the shared token and a cookie are unaffected.

environment.note: Three pod limits bear on what can be driven, none a defect of this change: gVisor answers SO_PEERPIDFD 'protocol not available', so agent-secrets-helper refuses every local client and a machine login must be driven as its four HTTP steps; Playwright's webkit and firefox cannot be installed, so only chromium rows run; and the whole internal/dispatch/api package takes longer than its CI job allows here (one of its rows, TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves, also fails for the pod's C collation rather than for the branch), so this round ran the fix's own test functions by name and left the whole package to CI, which owns it.
